3  JUDGMENT

These appeals have been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) by the claim petitioners and respondents 3 & 4 respectively in O.P.(MV) No.1670/2016 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Pathanamthitta, (the Tribunal), aggrieved by the Award dated 23/07/2019.
The respondents in MACA No.638/2020 are respondents 1 to 4 respectively in the petition and the respondents in MACA No.1005/2020 are claim petitioners 1 to 3 respectively in the petition.
In these appeals, the parties and documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioners, on 27/10/2015 at about 07:30 a.m. while the deceased was riding motorcycle bearing registration no.KL.51.B.8959 through Kottarakkara-Mavelikkara MC 2025:KER:73888 MACA NOS.638 & 1005 OF 2020 road and when he reached near the place by name Puthusseribhagam, car bearing registration no.KL.02.AU.5609 driven by the first respondent in a rash and negligent manner knocked him down, as a result of which he sustained grievous injuries to which he succumbed.
A sum of 60,00,000/- was claimed as compensation under various heads.
3. The first respondent/driver and the second respondent/owner of the offending vehicle filed written statement contending that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the deceased.
The age, occupation, employment and income of the deceased were disputed.
It was also contended that the compensation claimed was quite excessive.
4. The third respondent/insurer and the fourth respondent filed written statement admitting the existence of a valid policy in respect of the offending vehicle.
The age, occupation, employment and income of the deceased were disputed.
It was also contended that the compensation claimed was quite excessive.
Before the Tribunal, PW1 was examined and Exts.A1 to A40 were marked on the side of the claim petitioners.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.

6. The Tribunal on consideration of the oral and documentary evidence and after hearing both sides,
found negligence on the part of the first respondent/driver of the offending vehicle resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 27,04,830/- together with interest @ 9% per annum from the date of the petition till realisation along with proportionate costs.

Aggrieved by the Award,
the claim petitioners and respondents 3 and 4 have come up in appeal.
7. The only point that arises for consideration in these appeals is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.

8. Heard both sides Marykutty Eapen vs Arunkumar on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87949307/
4 9.
The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads is challenged - 2025:KER:73888 MACA NOS.638 & 1005 OF 2020
Notional income
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioners that the notional income fixed by the Tribunal as 20,000/- is quite low and the same needs to be enhanced.

It is submitted that in addition to an amount of 30,000/- that was being earned by the deceased, he was also getting gifts and hence the said aspect also ought to have been considered by the Tribunal and the notional income fixed accordingly.
Per contra, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the third respondent/insurer that the amount that has been fixed by the Tribunal is reasonable and that it does not call for any enhancement.
9.1. Though the claim is that the deceased was earning 30,000/-, there are no materials to support the same.
In such circumstances, the notional income of 20,000/- fixed by the Tribunal in the year 2015 appears to be just and reasonable.
Hence, no interference into the same is called for.
2025:KER:73888 MACA NOS.638 & 1005 OF 2020 Deduction to be made towards personal expenses 10.
Admittedly, the claim petitioners are the wife and two major children of the deceased.
The Tribunal has taken only the wife as the dependent as the two children are majors.
In the light of the dictum in Babita Singh v. New India Assurance Co. Ltd., 2024 ACJ 223, it is one third that is liable to be deducted and not one half as deducted by the Tribunal.

The accident took place on 27/10/2015 and the death took place on 25/07/2016.
Therefore, I find that he can be granted compensation towards loss of earnings for a period of 9 months, which comes to 1,80,000/- (20,000 x 9 months).

Based on Exts.A36 to A38, an amount of 39,150/- was claimed.
However, the Tribunal has granted 25,000/- only.
This is pointed out to be a mistake in adding up the amounts covered by 2025:KER:73888 MACA NOS.638 & 1005 OF 2020 the said documents.

12.1. A perusal of Exts.A36 to A38 cash vouchers show that amounts of 3,500/-, 6,150/- and 29,500/- were incurred, which comes to a total amount of 39,150/- out of which an amount of 25,000/- has been awarded.
Hence, the claim petitioners are entitled to the balance amount of 14,150/-.

The Tribunal has granted an amount of 40,000/- towards loss of consortium to the first claim petitioner and an amount of 25,000/-
each towards loss of love and affection to the second and third claim petitioners.
It is well settled that when compensation for loss of consortium is awarded, no further amount can be awarded for loss of love and affection.

The claim petitioners, three in number, are entitled to a total amount of 1,20,000/-, out of which an amount of 90,000/-, including the amount of 50,000/- under the wrong head of love and affection, has been granted.
Therefore, I find that they are entitled to the balance amount of 30,000/- towards loss of 2025:KER:73888 MACA NOS.638 & 1005 OF 2020 consortium.

15. The learned counsel for the third respondent/insurer draws my attention to paragraph no.21 of the impugned Award, the relevant portion of which reads thus:
"21........... For the treatment of the deceased the petitioners took a rented house near the hospital, and its vouchers produced, though it is not proved properly, an amount of Rs.30,000/- (Rs.10000x3 months) (Ext.A33 series) allowed under that head."
(Emphasis supplied)
The Tribunal despite finding that Ext.A33 series has not been proved has still allowed an amount of 30,000/- for which absolutely no reasons have been given.
Ext.A33 series has not been proved by any method known to law.
That being the position, I find that the Tribunal has wrongly awarded an amount of 30,000/-, which is liable to be deducted.
Medical expenses/Treatment expenses 16.

The learned counsel for the third respondent/insurer 2025:KER:73888 MACA NOS.638 & 1005 OF 2020 also objects to Exts.A20 to A23 and A25 and submits that the said amounts are also not due to the claim petitioners as the said amounts were paid by the sponsor, the Episcopal Church,
which is evident from the said documents itself.
Therefore, the claim petitioners are not entitled to the amounts covered by the said documents.

Per contra, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioners that the said fact has been clarified by PW1 while he was cross- examined and hence the Tribunal has not committed any mistake in awarding the amounts covered by the said Marykutty Eapen vs Arunkumar on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87949307/
6 documents.
16.1.
I was taken through the entire testimony of PW1 in which he has denied the allegation of the insurer that the amounts covered by Ext.A20 to A23 and A25 were paid by the Church.
There is no other evidence to the contrary.
In such circumstances, this Court is unable to accept the argument advanced by the learned counsel for the third respondent/insurer that these amounts were not paid by the claim petitioners.
